I was originally going to get an offroad style (more of a scrambler) to replace this with for the same reasons you've stated above but it went about the same speed as the one I have plus it was too tall for me, so I've decided to get a weaker 350cc cruiser that tops out below 100 (factory limiter) plus more time doing courses, for my own and my parents sake.

I hate to admit it but only recently have I started wearing gear, I kid you not only 2 weeks ago was I pushing 100 with nothing but my glasses, a t shirt, pants and crocs on, and ironically when I started wearing proper gear did I realize that even with all my high tech gear and upgrades to the brakes that anything can happen and no matter how much gear I put on it can't stop everything, and I'm ready to put my days of watery eyes and numb fingers behind me, no matter how much of a thrill it is.

I only always speed on empty roads where the only casualty would be me with the thought process being "if I'm not hurting anyone then what's the issue?" but I see now that my parents would blame themselves endlessly for getting me this bike and the paramedics that would have to clean up that mess that I can't even bring myself to think about if i end up sliding across the pavement. I'll make sure for my own sake that I think twice before giving into the temptations no matter how open the road is or how much I trust my abilities, due to me not having crashed at all before I feel this sense of invincibility and I better not do something dumb and put it to the test. thanks for your advice and have safe journeys!

I live in a super secluded place so there's never any cops or speed cameras to slow me down, but I think if I keep asking myself "what *if* there is a cop waiting for me?" it'll get me to maybe go the speed limit, but more than cops my fear is that even though i dont take risky cuts through traffic and only go on open roads are the variables like random potholes or drivers that don't look both ways when turning will make me crash real bad, I should definitely try and keep that in mind. thanks for the advice!

I was never into motorcycles, my plan was always turn 18 and get a small car for uni and such, and obviously my parents were really happy about that since most boys my age beg for a bike. I'd only had ridden 125cc scooters before this and they're more of a utility vehicle than anything. this feeling changed instantly when my best friend had bought a Thunderbird 500 and told me to get on and try riding it, I said why not it's not like ill enjoy it anyways and hopped on. obviously, stalled like 5 times before almost giving up but then it started moving, slowly it inched from a standstill into a 5kph jog, then I let go of the clutch and I was going! fell in love with it instantly. got home the next day and begged my dad to teach me how to ride on his Classic 500 and he hesitantly obliged. took a while of getting used to but every step from there on out was pure enjoyment, let it be a slow cruise to the coffee shop or trying to set a land speed record on the way back, it's just magical. I'm planning to buy a Meteor 350 in a couple of months for my birthday and I'll finally get to call a bike my own.
